citation: Lin W-D, et al. 'Metagenomic Next-Generation Sequencing in the identification of pathogens in hematologic patients with sepsis' (National Taiwan University Hospital), Microorganisms-type journal, 2021
study_design: Prospective observational cohort (mNGS vs conventional microbiology in haematologic patients with sepsis)

population.population_description: Adults (≥20 y) with haematologic malignancies and clinical sepsis (qSOFA criteria); infections: pneumonia 9/24 (37.5%), intra-abdominal 7/24 (29.2%), BSI 3/24 (12.5%), UTI 2/24 (8.4%); 14/24 neutropenic

neutropenic_status: 14 (58.3%) patients were diagnosed with neutropenia (absolute white blood cell < 500 cells/mm3) when sepsis developed

index_test.platform_or_panel: shotgun cfDNA mNGS on MGISEQ-200 (MGI Tech), Kraken2 bioinformatics, MGI in-house + RefSeq NCBI databases
index_test.dna_and_or_rna: DNA only (cfDNA; no RNA library described)

reference_standard: Clinical diagnosis of sepsis/infection (qSOFA + ID physician exclusion of non-infectious processes) with conventional microbiology (blood cultures, galactomannan, cryptococcal antigen, CMV RT-PCR, site-specific cultures/PCRs); no formal final-diagnosis adjudication against a composite reference reported

diagnostic_yield.basis: per-patient categories: 9 conventional equal to mNGS, 10 mNGS-only (additional pathogens), 3 conventional-only, 2 inconsistent; most mNGS detections were viruses

additional_yield_vs_conventional: Of ten patients, mNGS was able to identify additional pathogens compared with conventional methods; most of the pathogens were virus. Seven patients CMV detected by mNGS, only 3 confirmed CMV viremia by conventional PCR.
turnaround_time: Not timely available (time-consuming); specific TAT not reported. Interval between fever onset and mNGS sampling 0–4 days per patient.
therapy_change: Impact on antimicrobial administration unclear (results not timely available due to high cost and time-consuming data interpretation)

quality_flags.overlap_risk: no independent reference standard; positivity categories defined relative to conventional tests; colonisation/contamination acknowledged (e.g. B. cereus flagged as environmental contaminant by the pipeline yet confirmed bacteremic)

quadas2_notes: n=24, no 2x2 vs final diagnosis; yield data only. No mortality/TAT numbers. mNGS performed by commercial lab; DNA-only panel (RNA viruses potentially missed).

evidence_quotes.quote: From June 2019 to December 2019, we conducted a prospected study at National Taiwan University Hospital, which is a tertiary medical center with 2400-beds, located in northern Taiwan.
Fourteen (58.3%) patients were diagnosed with neutropenia (absolute white blood cell < 500 cells/mm 3 ) when sepsis developed.

Of 24 patients enrolled, mNGS and conventional diagnostic methods (blood cultures, serology testing and virus RT-PCR) reached comparable positive results in 9 cases. Of ten patients, mNGS was able to identify additional pathogens compared with conventional methods; most of the pathogens were virus.
Overall, CMV were detected among seven patients by mNGS; only three patients were confirmed with CMV viremia by conventional viral PCR.
Blood test for mNGS was performed within 24 h after the onset of a hypotension episode.

the results of mNGS were not timely available due to high cost and time-consuming data interpretation. Therefore, the impact of mNGS methods on the physicians' preference of antimicrobial agent administration remained unclear.
eight (35.7%) of 14 neutropenic patients obtain equal or more microbiologic evidence via mNGS, and of which five patients were documented with polymicrobial infection.

exclusion_reason: No 2x2 vs reference standard; comparison categories are relative to conventional testing only (yield-only).
